chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to us, from one, from Abi Tahir ibn Abi Hamza, from Abi al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

The temperaments are four: one is phlegm, and it is a stubborn adversary; and one is blood, and it is a servant, and perhaps the servant kills his master; and one is wind, and it is a king who is endured; and one is bile, and far, far is it like the earth when it trembles, it trembles with what is upon it.
ai.seo_question: What are the four temperaments described by Imam al-Rida in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the four primary humors (temperaments) in human physiology, using vivid metaphors to describe their behavioral influences: phlegm as a stubborn adversary, blood as a potentially rebellious servant, wind as a king to be managed, and bile as a destructive earth-shaker. This classification reflects the Greco-Arabic medical tradition (Unani) integrated into Shia hadith literature, offering practical insights into how physical constitution shapes character and health. The narration underscores the holistic Shia view of the human being, where physical humors directly impact spiritual and psychological states.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 32-11 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, on the authority of someone else, on the authority of Abi Tahir ibn Abi Hamza that Abil Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) said,

“There are four kinds of temperaments. One is phlegm that is a stubborn enemy. Then there is blood which is like Ethiopian servants who often kill their masters. The third one is the wind which is a king who puts up with his people and treats them gently. The last one is ‘Safra which is like the Earthquake which will make everything on the Earth tremble when it occurs.’”
